prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one floor of an old mine dungeon (timbered galleries dug into a mountain) in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: THE FIRST FLOOR OF AN OLD DEEP MINE: galleries of packed earth and grey-brown rock dug through dark stone, shored with heavy timber frames; a rail track for mine carts runs from the entrance in the south up the main gallery to a junction chamber and on east to a cart station at the edge of a deep vertical shaft, crossed only by a narrow rail trestle; a long drift west ends at a cave-in of fallen rock and splintered props; a small crevice nook; an ore-sorting room in the north with heaps of ore; beyond the shaft a gallery climbs north to the stairs down, and a long sloping gallery runs back south-west to the entrance hall. Palette: umber and grey-brown rock, timber browns, iron rails, black depths. Dusty, close, old.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 54 x 44 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2592 x 2112 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, rail, shore, cliff, wall, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, colour ramps, level of detail). Do NOT copy anything from it (no objects, signs or buildings from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles, triangles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give cliffs, rock walls, streams and meadows natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- light brown with arcs = the walkable mine FLOOR: packed earth and grey-brown rock of the galleries, cart ruts, small stones and ore crumbs, organic edges (never square or stepped).
- grey-brown with arcs = patches of loose GRAVEL / slag on the floor (walkable, flat).
- brown with steel lines = a RAIL TRACK for mine carts (walkable): dark wooden sleepers, two steel rails.
- brown with plank lines = TIMBER PLANKS: a boardwalk or a bridge of beams over a drop (walkable deck).
- teal = underground WATER (not walkable): dark still water with faint reflections.
- black = a deep CHASM / shaft (not walkable): a sheer drop into darkness.
- grey circles = BOULDERS, heaps of ore and rubble (not walkable).
- brown with vertical lines = TIMBER structures (not walkable): heavy wooden beams and props, scaffolds, sheds.
- very dark grey = solid ROCK (not walkable): the mountain's rock around the galleries, dark and jagged, seen from above, the sheer faces showing where it rises above the floor, streaked with ore veins; the gallery walls are shored with timber frames here and there; the outlines are natural and rounded, NEVER square, stepped or staircase-shaped; everything outside the floors is solid rock.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(140,100,62) = a narrow timber RAIL TRESTLE across the dark shaft: two rails on sleepers and a few beams, no planks to walk on.
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences, crates, carts or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo, NO vignette, NO fog over the map, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, mine carts on the rails, treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.

Create ONE complete finished 2592 x 2112 top-down fantasy JRPG old deep-mine first-floor GAME MAP. Do not design a new layout. Paint directly over the first reference's original boundaries: all tan connected walkable gallery shapes at their original widths; charcoal surrounding solid rock throughout; the dark vertical shaft near x=2100, y=380–1540; exactly-positioned east-west rail track from x~1280,y~1030 across the shaft on a narrow bare-sleeper timber rail trestle to x~2280,y~1030; track curving south at central junction x~1300,y~1100 and running down toward the bottom entrance at x~1270,y~2112. Preserve northwest dead-end chamber and its winding corridor to the central junction; north ore-sorting chamber at x~1000–1600,y~240–580 and its south-running access drift; far eastern tall north–south gallery with the upper chamber; the lower eastern gallery and its southwest-sloping return to the broad southern entrance hall. Preserve all guide's tight gaps, narrow corridor widths and winding boundaries, with only small organic edge irregularities. Where guide indicates circles, render exactly placed ore heaps/boulders; dead end/cave-in at the west end, splintered supports and rock debris only within their guide blocks. Everything outside walkable areas should remain solid jagged dark grey-brown mountain rock, clearly raised rough rock faces along organically curved walls, richly clustered rock fractures and muted mineral veins. Two steel rails, dark narrow sleepers, accurately following original track placement and original curvature; trestle over totally black vertical chasm has rails on sleepers and skeletal beams, NO solid walkable planking. The shaft remains the exact guide shape and pitch black. Premium modern hi-bit HAND-PLACED PIXEL ART: crisp square pixel clusters, muted hue-shifted tonal ramps, dark warm outlines, level of detail and visual pixel scale as SECOND reference; even neutral ambient daylight albedo, readable and moderately bright on walkable floor; not photorealistic, no painterly or smooth textures, no blur or antialiasing. Strict overhead RPG map with modest south-facing vertical rock faces, never isometric or 3D. No grid or labels, no text, no UI, no characters, no carts, no chests, no lanterns or lighting, no objects added blocking walkable paths, no border.
